_readme: Reference ranges and personal goals for `health` (the CLI view over health.db). Two different things, deliberately separate: `ref` is a clinical normal range — not a choice, it comes from published guidance — while `goal` is a value judgement about where you want to be, which no amount of data can derive. A metric can sit inside `ref` and still miss `goal`. Edit `goal` freely; changing `ref` means disagreeing with the cited source. Direction: 'higher' = more is better, 'lower' = less is better, 'band' = stay inside the range. Seeded from standard adult guidance; every entry cites where the number came from so a future reader can check it rather than trust it. These defaults assume a healthy adult — read each `why` before relying on one.

RestingHeartRate.label: Resting HR
RestingHeartRate.why: AHA calls 60-100 bpm normal for adults; athletes commonly 40-60. Sub-60 at rest is a fitness marker, so the goal is stricter than the clinical floor.

HeartRate.label: Heart rate (all-day avg)
HeartRate.why: All-day average mixes rest and activity, so no clinical range applies directly. Wide band flags only data problems or sustained tachycardia — read RestingHeartRate for signal.

HeartRateVariabilitySDNN.label: HRV (SDNN)
HeartRateVariabilitySDNN.why: SDNN is strongly age- and individual-dependent; absolute cutoffs are weak evidence. Population studies put healthy adult overnight SDNN around 40-100ms. Treat your own trend as the signal, not the number.

OxygenSaturation.label: Blood oxygen (SpO2)
OxygenSaturation.why: 95-100% is the standard normal for healthy adults at sea level; below 95 warrants attention, below 90 is hypoxemia. Wrist sensors read low on cold or poorly-perfused skin, so a single low value is usually artifact.

RespiratoryRate.label: Respiratory rate
RespiratoryRate.why: 12-20 breaths/min is the standard adult resting range. Sleep values run at or slightly below the low end.

StepCount.label: Daily steps
StepCount.why: Mortality benefit rises steeply to ~8000 steps/day and plateaus near 10000 (Paluch 2021, JAMA Netw Open). 8000 is where the curve flattens, so it is the honest target; 10000 was a 1960s pedometer slogan.

AppleExerciseTime.label: Exercise minutes
AppleExerciseTime.why: WHO recommends 150 min/week of moderate activity = ~21 min/day. The daily framing is a convenience; the weekly total is what the guidance actually says.

AppleStandHour.label: Stand hours
AppleStandHour.why: No clinical guideline exists; 12 is Apple's own default ring target and a reasonable proxy for breaking up sedentary time.

TimeInDaylight.label: Daylight
TimeInDaylight.why: Observational work links >2h/day outdoor light to better mood, sleep timing and myopia outcomes. Weaker evidence than the cardio numbers; treat as directional.

DistanceWalkingRunning.label: Walk+run distance
DistanceWalkingRunning.why: Roughly the distance implied by the 8000-step goal at an average adult step length (~65cm). Derived from the step goal, not independent guidance — recompute from your own WalkingStepLength if you care about the number.

SleepHours.label: Time asleep
SleepHours.why: AASM/Sleep Research Society consensus: 7+ hours per night for adults. `min_days` suppresses a verdict until 30 nights exist in the last 90 days, because sleep coverage is commonly poor: pre-watchOS-9 and third-party records log time in bed rather than sleep, and a watch that is charging overnight records nothing. Judging a night against a 7h goal from a stale fragment would invent a finding.

BodyMass.label: Weight
BodyMass.why: No universal target; BMI needs height and says little about composition. Tracked for trend only.

BodyFatPercentage.label: Body fat
BodyFatPercentage.why: ACE puts 'fitness' range at 14-17% and 'acceptable' at 18-24% for adult men; the corresponding bands for women run roughly 10 points higher. Set both ref and goal for your own body — this default is the male band.

VO2Max.label: VO2 max
VO2Max.why: Cooper Institute norms put 'good' for men 30-49 near 45 mL/kg/min; women's norms run about 8-10 mL/kg/min lower at the same age. One of the strongest single predictors of all-cause mortality, so worth a goal even on sparse data.

WalkingHeartRateAverage.label: Walking HR
WalkingHeartRateAverage.why: No clinical cutoff. A falling walking HR at constant pace is an aerobic-fitness signal, which is why it is tracked at all.

AppleWalkingSteadiness.label: Walking steadiness
AppleWalkingSteadiness.why: Apple's own bands: OK >=50%, Low 25-50%, Very Low <25%. Only meaningful as a fall-risk screen in older adults.

HeadphoneAudioExposure.label: Headphone audio
HeadphoneAudioExposure.why: WHO safe-listening: 80 dB for 40h/week for adults. Sustained exposure above that accumulates hearing damage.

EnvironmentalAudioExposure.label: Environment audio
EnvironmentalAudioExposure.why: Same WHO 80 dB basis as headphone exposure, applied to ambient sound.

FlightsClimbed.label: Flights climbed
FlightsClimbed.why: No guideline. Kept as a proxy for incidental vertical activity.

ActiveEnergyBurned.label: Active energy
ActiveEnergyBurned.why: Depends entirely on body mass and activity type; no population target is meaningful. Trend only.

BasalEnergyBurned.label: Basal energy
BasalEnergyBurned.why: A device estimate from body metrics, not a measurement. Useful only to notice sudden discontinuities.

systems._readme: Groups for the coverage matrix — which parts of the picture have data in which year. Grouping by body system makes gaps visible instead of leaving them implied by absence.
